description: FP8 KV cache (fp8_e4m3) vs BF16 KV cache, same strength-zero R30 checkpoint, same int6 embeddings (VLLM_EXL3_EMBED_ONLINE_BITS=6). Measures the KLD impact of FP8 KV cache quantization on the hidden-state output.

method.capture: fidelity.py capture, post-final-norm hook via collective_rpc (VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1), --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
method.replay: fidelity.py replay (direct, not R31 gate — gate requires BF16 KV), full-vocabulary KL(BF16||candidate), shared BF16 lm_head, 512 contexts x 2047 positions = 1,048,064 scored positions
method.note: R31 fidelity_gate.py rejects fp8_e4m3 KV cache because the frozen contract requires bfloat16. Replay was run directly with fidelity.py to measure the KV cache impact without the gate constraint.

model_loading_gib.note: Model loading is identical (~0.03 GiB difference is measurement noise). KV cache dtype affects KV cache pool size, not model weight loading.

kv_cache_log: Using fp8_e4m3 data type to store kv cache
conclusion: FP8 KV cache adds 0.000482 mean KLD (+14% over the BF16 KV control). The CI95s from the int6 control run were [0.003168, 0.003677]; the fp8kv mean 0.003891 is above that interval. This is a real fidelity cost, not noise. The tradeoff: FP8 KV roughly halves KV cache memory, enabling ~2x context length. Production already uses fp8_e4m3 KV cache in the throughput profile.
